text.p: Swiss brewer Feldschloesschen-Huerlimann Holding AG said it expected higher net and operating profit for the current 1996/1977 financial year and planned to introduce a single share.
"Thanks to considerable savings and higher earnings from properties we expect an improved operating and net profit," chief executive Gerard Stalder told a news conference.
Walter Hefti, chairman of the board, also said the brewer planned to introduce a single registered share.
"The concentration on registered shares as the only share category will significantly improve liquidity," Hefti said.

The group, created by the merger of Feldschloesschen and Huerlimann breweries as of January 1 1996, made a loss of 113 million Swiss francs after restructuring charges in the 1995/96 financial year that ended September 30.
Group operating profit last year was 51 million francs.
Total restructuring costs of 315 milliion francs expected until the end of 1998 were booked against the 1995/96 results.
